profile.research_note: [batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This CoreSite facility is in one of the company confirmed operating markets. Wikipedia coverage states that as of June 2022 CoreSite operated 27 data center facilities across 10 markets totaling over 4.6 million net rentable square feet, with key locations including Boston, Chicago, Denver, Los Angeles, Miami, New York City, Northern Virginia, San Francisco/San Jose, Santa Clara, Atlanta, Orlando, and Washington, D.C. In May 2007 the company acquired Chicago properties as part of a wider expansion. CoreSite began operating a Washington, D.C. facility in August 2005, one of its earliest East Coast sites after founding in 2001 as CRG West. CoreSite rebranded from CRG West to CoreSite in June 2009, went public in September 2010, and was acquired by American Tower in December 2021. This specific market was confirmed as an active CoreSite location, but no market specific acquisition date or building history beyond the general company timeline was located in available sourcing this session.

reading.body:
The CoreSite Secaucus Campus publishes 256,000 square feet of technical space but no IT load figure in megawatts. Without a published power number, no rack or accelerator estimate can be derived, and this campus does not contribute to New Jersey's 94 MW total across the three facilities on this site that have published a figure. That absence of a power specification is the most significant thing the page does not say, because for AI workloads power density, not floor area alone, determines how many accelerators a facility can sustain.

The certifications qualify this campus to host financially audited workloads (SOC 1 Type 2), security-audited workloads (SOC 2 Type 2), payment card data (PCI DSS), protected health information (HIPAA), internationally benchmarked information security controls (ISO 27001), and US federal security framework workloads (NIST 800-53). Taken together, those certifications cover most regulated enterprise and government use cases. They say nothing about the power density or cooling architecture that AI training and inference demand.

New Jersey has 47 mapped facilities in this site's dataset, of which only 3 publish a megawatt figure. This campus ranks fourth by published megawatts in the state, which in practice means it ranks below the three that publish any number at all. That ranking reflects a data gap as much as a capacity gap. New Jersey sits across the Hudson from one of the densest fiber interconnection points in the United States, which gives any campus there a structural latency advantage for inference serving, but whether this campus can deliver the power density that AI training requires is not answerable from what the operator has published.
